insights.description: Incorrect plural form: 'student' vs 'students'
insights.title: Plural Nouns: Use of 'student' instead of 'students'
insights.original_text: Because all student wear same clothes
insights.suggested_text: Because all students wear the same clothes

insights.description: Incorrect verb form: 'like wear' instead of 'like wearing'
insights.title: Incorrect Verb Form: 'like wear' vs 'like wearing'
insights.original_text: I like wear my own clothes
insights.suggested_text: I like wearing my own clothes

insights.description: Incorrect sentence structure: 'uniform is not comfortable in summer is very hot'
insights.title: Compound Sentence Errors: Incorrect conjunction use
insights.original_text: uniform is not comfortable in summer is very hot
insights.suggested_text: The uniform is not comfortable in summer because it is very hot

insights.description: Inaccurate preposition: 'cheaper for parent' should be 'cheaper for parents'
insights.title: Plural Agreement with Prepositions
insights.original_text: is cheaper for parent
insights.suggested_text: is cheaper for parents

insights.description: Lack of academic vocabulary: 'good', 'same clothes', 'better'
insights.title: Limited Academic Vocabulary
insights.original_text: I think school uniform is good. Because all student wear same clothes and no one is poor or rich
insights.suggested_text: I believe school uniforms promote equality, as they reduce social distinctions between students

insights.description: Limited development of ideas with only two main points, lacking depth and elaboration.
insights.title: Shallow Argument Development
insights.original_text: In my opinion, school uniforms are a good idea for several reasons. First, they make all students look equal, so nobody feels bad about their clothes. Second, parents don't need to buy many expensive clothes every year.
insights.suggested_text: In my opinion, school uniforms are a good idea for several reasons. First, they promote equality by reducing social differences in appearance, which helps foster a sense of belonging among students. Second, they reduce financial burdens on families, especially those with limited income, by eliminating the need for students to purchase multiple costly outfits annually.

insights.description: Use of simple sentence structures with few complex or varied constructions.
insights.title: Limited Grammatical Variety
insights.original_text: However, some students say uniforms are uncomfortable and they cannot show their personality. I agree that this is a problem, but I think the advantages are more important.
insights.suggested_text: However, some students argue that uniforms are uncomfortable and restrict personal expression. While this concern is valid, the benefits of uniform policies—such as promoting discipline and reducing peer pressure—outweigh these drawbacks.

insights.description: Repetition of basic vocabulary; limited use of academic or formal phrases.
insights.title: Underdeveloped Lexical Range
insights.original_text: they make all students look equal, so nobody feels bad about their clothes. parents don't need to buy many expensive clothes every year.
insights.suggested_text: uniforms help create a sense of equality among students, minimizing feelings of social exclusion. Families also avoid significant annual spending on clothing, which is especially beneficial in low-income households.

insights.description: Inconsistent punctuation and minor errors in article and preposition use.
insights.title: Punctuation and Article Errors
insights.original_text: I agree that this is a problem, but I think the advantages are more important. So, I think schools should keep uniforms.
insights.suggested_text: I acknowledge this concern, but I believe the overall advantages—such as improved discipline and reduced social comparison—justify the implementation of school uniforms. Therefore, I recommend that schools maintain uniform policies.

insights.description: Use of clear position and argument structure
insights.title: Clear Position Statement and Structure
insights.original_text: While some argue that school uniforms restrict individuality, I largely agree that they should be compulsory.
insights.suggested_text: While some argue that school uniforms limit individual expression, I largely agree that they should be mandatory.

insights.description: Limited range of vocabulary; overuse of simple phrases
insights.title: Overreliance on Basic Vocabulary
insights.original_text: Firstly, uniforms reduce social pressure, as students cannot compete over expensive brands.
insights.suggested_text: Firstly, uniforms reduce social pressures by eliminating competition over costly fashion items.

insights.description: Grammatical accuracy with minor errors in preposition and word choice
insights.title: Inaccurate Preposition and Word Choice
insights.original_text: admittedly, self-expression matters, yet students can still express themselves through hobbies and friendships.
insights.suggested_text: While self-expression is important, students can still express themselves through extracurricular activities and personal relationships.

insights.description: Lack of development in argumentation and depth
insights.title: Shallow Argument Development
insights.original_text: In conclusion, the benefits of uniforms outweigh their drawbacks.
insights.suggested_text: In conclusion, the educational and social benefits of school uniforms significantly outweigh the limited drawbacks, especially in promoting equality and reducing financial strain on families.

insights.description: Use of abstract academic vocabulary can be effective but may lack clarity or accessibility for some readers. Overuse of terms like 'conspicuous consumption' or 'socioeconomic divides' without clear explanation can confuse the reader.
insights.title: Precision in Academic Vocabulary
insights.original_text: neutralise the conspicuous consumption that otherwise taints adolescent peer relations
insights.suggested_text: reduce the emphasis on expensive clothing that can create social divisions among students

insights.description: The phrase 'levels the field' is idiomatic but vague. It requires explanation to ensure clarity and avoid ambiguity in meaning.
insights.title: Idiomatic Expressions Need Clarification
insights.original_text: a standardised dress code, by contrast, levels the field without suppressing character
insights.suggested_text: a standardised dress code helps equalise students' appearance, so that differences in background do not influence peer relationships

insights.description: The expression 'character finds its outlet in conversation, creativity and conduct' is grammatically correct but conceptually unclear. 'Character' here is ambiguous—does it mean moral character or personal traits? This needs refinement to avoid confusion.
insights.title: Ambiguity in Conceptual Use of Key Terms
insights.original_text: character tends to find its outlet in conversation, creativity and conduct rather than in clothing
insights.suggested_text: students' individuality is better expressed through conversation, creativity, and personal behaviour, not through clothing

insights.description: The sentence structure is complex and varied, demonstrating good grammatical range. However, a few clauses are overlong and could be broken into simpler sentences for better readability.
insights.title: Balancing Complexity with Readability
insights.original_text: Where pupils are visibly differentiated by brand, schools inadvertently entrench socioeconomic divides; a standardised dress code, by contrast, levels the field without suppressing character, which tends to find its outlet in conversation, creativity and conduct rather than in clothing.
insights.suggested_text: When students are visibly marked by brand names, schools can reinforce social divisions based on income. In contrast, a uniform helps equalise appearance, allowing students to express themselves through conversation, creativity, and behaviour—rather than through clothing.

insights.description: Simple sentence structures with no complex clauses or linking words
insights.title: Lack of complex sentence structures
insights.original_text: You can sleep more and no traffic.
insights.suggested_text: You can sleep more and avoid traffic, which saves time and improves your daily routine.

insights.description: Inappropriate or vague vocabulary (e.g., 'is bad too', 'no talk with friends')
insights.title: Inaccurate and unprecise vocabulary
insights.original_text: But is bad too, because you are alone and no talk with friends.
insights.suggested_text: However, it has disadvantages such as social isolation and reduced opportunities for professional interaction.

insights.description: No clear structure or development of ideas (no introduction, body, conclusion)
insights.title: Missing essay structure
insights.original_text: Many people work at home now. It is good because you not need go to office. You can sleep more and no traffic. But is bad too... I think work at home is good one or two day in week.
insights.suggested_text: Nowadays, many people work from home. This trend has both advantages and disadvantages. On the one hand, it offers flexibility and eliminates commuting. On the other hand, it can lead to social isolation and work-life imbalance. Therefore, a balanced approach—such as working from home one or two days a week—may be ideal.

insights.description: Inconsistent grammar and tense errors (e.g., 'you not need', 'I can't work')
insights.title: Incorrect verb forms and word order
insights.original_text: You not need go to office. Sometimes the children make noise and I can't work.
insights.suggested_text: You no longer need to go to an office. Sometimes, children's noise interferes with concentration and productivity.

insights.description: Limited range of vocabulary and use of basic, repetitive phrases
insights.title: Narrow vocabulary range
insights.original_text: It is good because you not need go to office. I think work at home is good one or two day in week.
insights.suggested_text: Working from home provides benefits such as time savings and improved work-life balance, but it may also result in reduced communication and lack of motivation.

insights.description: Use of clear topic sentences and logical structure
insights.title: Clear Structure with Balanced Advantages and Disadvantages
insights.original_text: One advantage is that they save time and money because they don't have to travel to the office. Another advantage is that they can organise their day more freely.
insights.suggested_text: One major advantage is that employees save time and money by eliminating commuting. Another benefit is greater flexibility in scheduling, allowing individuals to structure their workday according to their personal routines.

insights.description: Use of weak linking and overgeneralized expressions
insights.title: Inadequate Transition Between Ideas
insights.original_text: On the other hand, working at home can be lonely and some people find it difficult to separate work and private life.
insights.suggested_text: However, working from home can lead to social isolation and difficulty in maintaining a clear boundary between professional and personal time.

insights.description: Limited vocabulary range and use of simple, repetitive phrases
insights.title: Limited Lexical Range – Overuse of Basic Collocations
insights.original_text: they save time and money because they don't have to travel to the office
insights.suggested_text: they save time and money by eliminating daily commutes

insights.description: Inaccurate or unidiomatic sentence structures
insights.title: Incorrect Preposition and Article Use
insights.original_text: they can organise their day more freely
insights.suggested_text: they can organise their daily work schedule more flexibly

insights.description: Inconsistent verb tenses and weak expression of opinion
insights.title: Inconsistent Tense and Lack of Nuance in Opinion
insights.original_text: In my opinion, the best solution is to work at home some days and in the office on other days.
insights.suggested_text: In my view, a balanced approach—working from home on some days and visiting the office on others—would offer the best compromise between flexibility and social interaction.

insights.description: Use of sophisticated vocabulary with academic tone
insights.title: Sophisticated Lexical Choice
insights.original_text: the tyranny of the commute
insights.suggested_text: the burden of commuting

insights.description: Precision in argumentation with balanced structure
insights.title: Balanced Advantages and Disadvantages
insights.original_text: Undoubtedly, flexibility enhances autonomy... Conversely, the erosion of informal interaction... can quietly impoverish organisational culture
insights.suggested_text: One major advantage is increased flexibility, which improves work-life balance. However, a key disadvantage is the loss of spontaneous workplace interactions that foster team cohesion.

insights.description: Complex sentence structures with varied syntax
insights.title: Use of Subordinate Clauses and Compound Structures
insights.original_text: while the absence of physical boundaries tempts employees to be perpetually available
insights.suggested_text: The lack of physical separation often leads to employees feeling pressured to respond to work messages at all times.

insights.description: Precision in logical flow and topic development
insights.title: Clear Logical Progression
insights.original_text: A deliberately structured hybrid model therefore seems preferable to either extreme.
insights.suggested_text: Given the trade-offs, a well-designed hybrid model offers a balanced solution that combines the benefits of remote and in-office work.

insights.description: Basic sentence structure and subject-verb agreement errors
insights.title: Subject-Verb Agreement and Basic Sentence Structure
insights.original_text: Bus and train is good for people because is cheap.
insights.suggested_text: Buses and trains are good for people because they are cheap.

insights.description: Inappropriate or unidiomatic word choices
insights.title: Inaccurate and Unnatural Vocabulary Use
insights.original_text: Many people have not car.
insights.suggested_text: Many people do not own a car.

insights.description: Lack of logical development and argument structure
insights.title: Underdeveloped Argument and Missing Evidence
insights.original_text: In my city the bus is old and slow, so people don't like it. Government should buy new bus.
insights.suggested_text: In my city, the bus system is outdated and inefficient, leading to low public trust. Therefore, the government should invest in modern, reliable public transport to improve accessibility and reduce traffic congestion.

insights.description: Failure to address the prompt fully or balance opinion
insights.title: Failure to Address the 'Extent' of the Issue
insights.original_text: I think government must spend more money for public transport.
insights.suggested_text: While I agree that governments should prioritize public transport, I believe this should be balanced with investment in road infrastructure to ensure safety and efficiency, especially in urban areas.

insights.description: Missing coherence and linking devices
insights.title: Lack of Cohesion with Linking Words
insights.original_text: Roads are important too but too many car make air bad and traffic jam.
insights.suggested_text: Roads are important, but when too many cars are on the road, air quality deteriorates and traffic congestion increases.

insights.description: Limited development of ideas; response is surface-level and lacks depth or critical analysis.
insights.title: Shallow Argument Development
insights.original_text: I believe governments should spend more money on public transport than on roads. Firstly, public transport is cheaper for ordinary people, and it helps to reduce traffic jams. Secondly, fewer cars means less pollution, which is good for health.
insights.suggested_text: I believe governments should prioritize public transport over road construction. Public transport offers a cost-effective alternative for individuals, reducing reliance on private vehicles and easing congestion. Moreover, widespread public transport use can significantly lower carbon emissions, contributing to improved air quality and public health.

insights.description: Frequent use of simple sentence structures with no complex or varied sentence types.
insights.title: Limited Sentence Variety
insights.original_text: Firstly, public transport is cheaper for ordinary people, and it helps to reduce traffic jams. Secondly, fewer cars means less pollution, which is good for health.
insights.suggested_text: Public transport not only reduces individual expenses but also alleviates traffic congestion. With fewer cars on the road, urban air pollution decreases, leading to better public health outcomes and reduced environmental degradation.

insights.description: Use of vague or simplistic vocabulary; lacks academic or formal register.
insights.title: Underdeveloped Lexical Range
insights.original_text: public transport is cheaper for ordinary people
insights.suggested_text: public transport is more affordable for the average citizen

insights.description: Lack of logical transitions and clear paragraph structure; ideas are presented in a list format without flow.
insights.title: Weak Paragraph Flow
insights.original_text: Firstly, public transport is cheaper for ordinary people, and it helps to reduce traffic jams. Secondly, fewer cars means less pollution, which is good for health. Of course, roads are still necessary, for example for ambulances and delivery trucks.
insights.suggested_text: While public transport offers significant economic and environmental benefits, roads remain essential for emergency services and delivery logistics. However, expanding road infrastructure may inadvertently encourage more car ownership, undermining long-term congestion and pollution reduction goals.

insights.description: Inaccurate or unbalanced reasoning; fails to address the 'extent' of the statement or consider counterarguments.
insights.title: Failure to Address 'Extent' of the Statement
insights.original_text: But if the government builds more roads, there will be more cars, so the problem will not disappear.
insights.suggested_text: While expanding roads may seem beneficial in the short term, it often leads to induced demand—where more roads attract more drivers—thereby perpetuating congestion and pollution. Therefore, investment in public transport offers a more sustainable long-term solution.

insights.description: Unclear conclusion; does not synthesize the argument or reflect on the broader implications.
insights.title: Underdeveloped Conclusion
insights.original_text: For these reasons I agree with the statement.
insights.suggested_text: In conclusion, prioritizing public transport over road expansion aligns with both economic efficiency and environmental sustainability, making it a more effective long-term policy for urban development.

insights.description: Clear position and balanced reasoning with a well-structured argument
insights.title: Strong Position with Balanced View
insights.original_text: I broadly share this view.
insights.suggested_text: I agree with this perspective to a significant extent.

insights.description: Effective use of contrast and logical transitions
insights.title: Effective Use of Contrast and Transitions
insights.original_text: However, some investment in roads remains essential...
insights.suggested_text: That said, road investment remains necessary, especially in rural areas where alternatives are limited.

insights.description: Precise and academic vocabulary
insights.title: Accurate and Appropriate Vocabulary
insights.original_text: efficient buses and trains can move far more people with less pollution
insights.suggested_text: efficient public transit systems can carry significantly more people while reducing emissions.

insights.description: Clear and varied sentence structures
insights.title: Varied Sentence Structures with Appropriate Complexity
insights.original_text: Building additional roads tends to encourage more car use, so congestion soon returns
insights.suggested_text: The construction of new roads often leads to increased car usage, which in turn exacerbates traffic congestion.

insights.description: Use of a clear conclusion that synthesizes the argument
insights.title: Strong Conclusion with Synthesis
insights.original_text: On balance, priority should be given to public transport.
insights.suggested_text: Therefore, public transport should be prioritized in government spending allocations.

insights.description: Clear position and balanced argument with a nuanced view.
insights.title: Nuanced Positioning
insights.original_text: Whether public money is better channelled into public transport or road infrastructure is, in my view, less a question of either/or than of strategic emphasis, though the evidence favours the former.
insights.suggested_text: In my view, the debate over whether governments should spend more on public transport or roads is not a simple choice between two options, but rather a matter of strategic prioritization—especially given that evidence supports a greater investment in public transport.

insights.description: Subject-verb agreement error
insights.title: Subject-Verb Agreement
insights.original_text: Because all student wear same clothes
insights.suggested_text: Because all students wear the same clothes

insights.description: Incorrect verb form (like wear vs. wearing)
insights.title: Incorrect Verb Form (Infinitive vs. Gerund)
insights.original_text: I like wear my own clothes
insights.suggested_text: I like wearing my own clothes

insights.description: Incorrect plural form (parent vs. parents)
insights.title: Plural Noun Error
insights.original_text: is cheaper for parent
insights.suggested_text: is cheaper for parents

insights.description: Inaccurate generalization ('no one is poor or rich')
insights.title: Misleading Generalization
insights.original_text: no one is poor or rich
insights.suggested_text: it helps reduce social differences and promotes equality

insights.description: Lack of academic vocabulary and range
insights.title: Limited Lexical Range
insights.original_text: I think school uniform is good. Because all student wear same clothes and no one is poor or rich.
insights.suggested_text: Wearing school uniforms promotes equality among students and reduces financial disparities in school settings.

insights.description: Weak logical flow and transitions
insights.title: Poor Logical Flow
insights.original_text: But sometimes uniform is not comfortable in summer is very hot. I like wear my own clothes but I think uniform is better for school.
insights.suggested_text: However, uniforms may become uncomfortable in hot weather. While I personally prefer wearing my own clothes, I believe uniforms contribute more to a sense of discipline and unity in school.

insights.description: Missing balanced argument and development
insights.title: Unbalanced Argument
insights.original_text: I think school uniform is good. ... I like it.
insights.suggested_text: While school uniforms have benefits such as promoting equality and reducing financial burdens, they also present challenges like discomfort in extreme weather. Therefore, a balanced approach may be needed.

insights.description: Grammar: Use of linking devices
insights.title: Improve transition phrases for academic tone
insights.original_text: However, some students say uniforms are uncomfortable and they cannot show their personality.
insights.suggested_text: On the other hand, some students argue that uniforms can be uncomfortable and limit personal expression.

insights.description: Vocabulary: Idiomatic expression in academic writing
insights.title: Replace informal expressions with academic precision
insights.original_text: nobody feels bad about their clothes
insights.suggested_text: students may feel less self-conscious about their appearance

insights.description: Style: Development of argument
insights.title: Strengthen argument with comparative reasoning
insights.original_text: I agree that this is a problem, but I think the advantages are more important.
insights.suggested_text: While personal expression is important, the benefits of promoting equality and reducing financial burdens on families outweigh these concerns.

insights.description: Lexical Resource: Precision and range
insights.title: Use more formal and specific phrasing
insights.original_text: parents don't need to buy many expensive clothes every year
insights.suggested_text: families can avoid significant annual spending on clothing

insights.description: Coherence: Logical connection between ideas
insights.title: Improve logical flow between claims
insights.original_text: First, they make all students look equal, so nobody feels bad about their clothes.
insights.suggested_text: uniforms help reduce social comparisons, which can prevent students from feeling inferior due to differences in clothing.

insights.description: Grammar: Preposition use in idiomatic expressions
insights.title: Improve idiomatic prepositions in comparisons
insights.original_text: students cannot compete over expensive brands
insights.suggested_text: students cannot compete for expensive clothing

insights.description: Vocabulary: Use of precise and formal alternatives
insights.title: Replace informal phrases with formal equivalents
insights.original_text: save families money in the long run, because children need fewer outfits
insights.suggested_text: reduce household expenses over time, as children require fewer clothing items

insights.description: Style: Strengthen conclusion with a more impactful closing
insights.title: Elevate conclusion to reinforce argument more effectively
insights.original_text: In conclusion, the benefits of uniforms outweigh their drawbacks.
insights.suggested_text: In conclusion, the advantages of school uniforms—such as promoting equality and reducing financial burdens—far outweigh their limitations, making them a worthwhile policy for schools.

insights.description: Lexical resource: Use of precise academic vocabulary
insights.title: Introduce academic terms to enhance precision
insights.original_text: a more inclusive atmosphere
insights.suggested_text: a more inclusive and equitable learning environment

insights.description: Grammar: Sentence structure variety and complexity
insights.title: Develop varied sentence structures for natural flow
insights.original_text: Admittedly, self-expression matters, yet students can still express themselves through hobbies and friendships.
insights.suggested_text: While self-expression is important, students can still demonstrate individuality through extracurricular activities and personal relationships.

insights.description: Use of sophisticated academic vocabulary with precision
insights.title: Precision in Academic Vocabulary
insights.original_text: The debate over compulsory school uniforms invariably pits the virtue of collective identity against the freedom of self-expression.
insights.suggested_text: The debate over school uniforms often contrasts the value of group identity with individual expression.

insights.description: Effective use of complex sentence structures with subordinate clauses
insights.title: Complex Sentence Structure and Subordination
insights.original_text: Where pupils are visibly differentiated by brand, schools inadvertently entrench socioeconomic divides; a standardised dress code, by contrast, levels the field without suppressing character...
insights.suggested_text: When students are visibly distinguished by brand, schools unintentionally reinforce social inequalities; in contrast, a uniform dress code creates equality without diminishing personal character.

insights.description: Appropriate use of logical connectors and transitions
insights.title: Logical Flow and Transition
insights.original_text: That said, uniforms should be affordable and climate-appropriate, lest the policy itself become a financial burden.
insights.suggested_text: However, uniforms must be affordable and suitable for the climate, otherwise the policy may become a financial strain on families.

insights.description: Clarity and coherence of argument despite brevity
insights.title: Concise, Coherent Argument Structure
insights.original_text: Although I acknowledge the latter's merit, I am inclined to side with uniforms...
insights.suggested_text: While I recognize the value of personal expression, I believe uniforms are more beneficial for students.

insights.description: Basic sentence structures with no variety or complexity
insights.title: Limited grammatical range and structure
insights.original_text: You not need go to office.
insights.suggested_text: You do not need to go to the office.

insights.description: Inappropriate or incorrect word forms (e.g., 'is bad too')
insights.title: Incorrect verb forms and article usage
insights.original_text: But is bad too, because you are alone and no talk with friends.
insights.suggested_text: However, it is also bad because you are alone and cannot talk to friends.

insights.description: Inadequate vocabulary for academic writing (e.g., 'I can't work')
insights.title: Underdeveloped and informal vocabulary
insights.original_text: Sometimes the children make noise and I can't work.
insights.suggested_text: Sometimes, children's noise interferes with my ability to work effectively.

insights.description: Lack of logical progression and development of ideas
insights.title: Weak idea development and argument structure
insights.original_text: I think work at home is good one or two day in week.
insights.suggested_text: I believe working from home should be limited to one or two days per week to balance productivity and social interaction.

insights.description: Missing clear structure: introduction, body, conclusion
insights.title: Absence of paragraph structure and logical flow
insights.original_text: Many people work at home now. It is good because you not need go to office. You can sleep more and no traffic. But is bad too, because you are alone and no talk with friends. Sometimes the children make noise and I can't work. I think work at home is good one or two day in week.
insights.suggested_text: Many people now work from home. This trend has both advantages and disadvantages. On the positive side, it saves time and allows individuals to sleep more and avoid traffic. However, working from home can lead to social isolation, lack of interaction with colleagues, and distractions such as household noise. Therefore, a balanced approach—limiting home work to one or two days per week—may be most effective.

insights.description: Lack of paragraph structure
insights.title: Missing Paragraphing
insights.original_text: Nowadays more and more people work from home. One advantage is that they save time and money because they don't have to travel to the office. Another advantage is that they can organise their day more freely. On the other hand, working at home can be lonely and some people find it difficult to separate work and private life. In my opinion, the best solution is to work at home some days and in the office on other days.
insights.suggested_text: Nowadays, more and more people work from home. This trend has both benefits and drawbacks. First, working from home saves time and money because individuals no longer need to travel to an office. It also allows people to better organise their daily schedule. On the other hand, working from home can lead to loneliness and difficulty in separating work from personal life. Therefore, a balanced approach—such as working from home some days and in the office on others—may offer the best solution.

insights.description: Limited grammatical range
insights.title: Overuse of simple sentences
insights.original_text: Nowadays more and more people work from home. One advantage is that they save time and money because they don't have to travel to the office. Another advantage is that they can organise their day more freely.
insights.suggested_text: Nowadays, more and more people work from home. This allows them to save time and money, as they no longer need to commute to an office. It also enables greater flexibility in planning their workday.

insights.description: Inaccurate or awkward phrasing
insights.title: Awkward solution sentence
insights.original_text: In my opinion, the best solution is to work at home some days and in the office on other days.
insights.suggested_text: Therefore, a balanced approach—such as working from home on some days and visiting the office on others—could be the most effective solution.

insights.description: Limited lexical variety
insights.title: Basic vocabulary with no synonyms
insights.original_text: they save time and money because they don't have to travel to the office
insights.suggested_text: they save time and money by eliminating daily commutes

insights.description: Lack of critical analysis
insights.title: Superficial discussion of disadvantages
insights.original_text: working at home can be lonely and some people find it difficult to separate work and private life
insights.suggested_text: working from home can lead to social isolation and blurred boundaries between professional and personal time

insights.description: Use of varied sentence structures to improve range and complexity
insights.title: Sentence Variety and Complexity
insights.original_text: Remote working has become increasingly common, and it brings both benefits and drawbacks.
insights.suggested_text: The rise of remote work has led to both significant advantages and notable challenges in the modern workplace.

insights.description: Precision in vocabulary choice to convey nuanced ideas
insights.title: Precision in Academic Vocabulary
insights.original_text: workers may feel isolated from colleagues
insights.suggested_text: employees may experience social disconnection or a sense of professional isolation

insights.description: Clarity in linking ideas with cohesive devices
insights.title: Effective Use of Transition and Linking
insights.original_text: Nevertheless, there are notable disadvantages.
insights.suggested_text: However, such flexibility comes at a cost, including potential social disconnection and diminished team cohesion.

insights.description: Improved flow through logical progression of ideas
insights.title: Logical Flow and Argument Development
insights.original_text: Overall, I believe a hybrid arrangement offers the most sensible balance, since it preserves flexibility without sacrificing teamwork.
insights.suggested_text: Therefore, a hybrid model—combining remote work with in-person meetings—provides the most balanced solution, preserving flexibility while maintaining team collaboration.

insights.description: Avoiding vague or overused expressions
insights.title: Avoiding Overused Phrases
insights.original_text: it brings both benefits and drawbacks
insights.suggested_text: it presents a range of advantages and disadvantages

insights.description: Subject-verb agreement error in simple sentences
insights.title: Subject-Verb Agreement Error
insights.original_text: Bus and train is good for people because is cheap.
insights.suggested_text: Buses and trains are good for people because they are cheap.

insights.description: Incorrect article usage and word form
insights.title: Incorrect Article and Word Form
insights.original_text: many people have not car
insights.suggested_text: many people do not have a car

insights.description: Incorrect plural form and collocation
insights.title: Incorrect Plural and Collocation
insights.original_text: too many car make air bad and traffic jam
insights.suggested_text: too many cars make the air bad and cause traffic jams

insights.description: Lack of logical progression and transitional phrases
insights.title: Poor Flow and Transitions
insights.original_text: In my city the bus is old and slow, so people don't like it. Government should buy new bus.
insights.suggested_text: In my city, buses are old and slow, so many people do not use them. Therefore, the government should invest in new, modern buses.

insights.description: Limited range of vocabulary and topic-specific terminology
insights.title: Limited Lexical Range
insights.original_text: government must spend more money for public transport
insights.suggested_text: governments should prioritize investment in public transportation systems

insights.description: No clear argument structure or development of position
insights.title: Underdeveloped Argument Structure
insights.original_text: I think government must spend more money for public transport.
insights.suggested_text: While roads are essential, I believe governments should allocate a greater portion of their transportation budget to public transport because it promotes equity, reduces pollution, and supports sustainable urban development.

insights.description: Limited range of grammatical structures – relies heavily on simple sentences and basic linking words.
insights.title: Simple Sentence Structure and Limited Linking
insights.original_text: I believe governments should spend more money on public transport than on roads. Firstly, public transport is cheaper for ordinary people, and it helps to reduce traffic jams. Secondly, fewer cars means less pollution, which is good for health.
insights.suggested_text: I believe that governments should prioritize public transport over road infrastructure. Public transport is significantly more affordable for ordinary citizens, and by reducing private car usage, it helps alleviate traffic congestion. Furthermore, fewer vehicles on the road lead to lower levels of air pollution, which has direct positive effects on public health.

insights.description: Repetition of basic vocabulary; limited use of academic or nuanced terms.
insights.title: Basic and Repetitive Vocabulary
insights.original_text: public transport is cheaper for ordinary people, and it helps to reduce traffic jams. Secondly, fewer cars means less pollution, which is good for health.
insights.suggested_text: Public transport offers a cost-effective alternative for individuals, helping to reduce traffic congestion. Reduced car dependency results in lower emissions, improving environmental and public health outcomes.

insights.description: Lack of development in argument – points are stated but not fully explained or expanded.
insights.title: Underdeveloped Reasoning and Analysis
insights.original_text: But if the government builds more roads, there will be more cars, so the problem will not disappear.
insights.suggested_text: If governments invest in road expansion, it may inadvertently encourage increased car ownership, leading to a cycle of congestion and pollution that undermines long-term urban sustainability.

insights.description: Inconsistent use of pronouns and references – unclear antecedents or logical flow.
insights.title: Ambiguous Reference and Pronoun Use
insights.original_text: Of course, roads are still necessary, for example for ambulances and delivery trucks. But if the government builds more roads, there will be more cars, so the problem will not disappear.
insights.suggested_text: While roads remain essential for emergency services and commercial deliveries, expanding road networks may encourage greater private vehicle use, thereby perpetuating traffic congestion and environmental degradation.

insights.description: Clear stance and balanced argument with logical progression
insights.title: Clear Position and Balanced View
insights.original_text: I broadly share this view.
insights.suggested_text: I agree with the view that governments should prioritize public transport over road construction.

insights.description: Use of cause-effect reasoning and logical transitions
insights.title: Effective Cause-Effect Linking
insights.original_text: Building additional roads tends to encourage more car use, so congestion soon returns...
insights.suggested_text: Expanding road networks often leads to induced demand, where more people buy cars to access the new roads, resulting in congestion that quickly returns.

insights.description: Use of a clear contrast between public transport and roads
insights.title: Precise Contrast of Public Transport vs. Roads
insights.original_text: whereas efficient buses and trains can move far more people with less pollution.
insights.suggested_text: in contrast, efficient buses and trains can transport significantly more people with far less environmental impact.

insights.description: Limited range of vocabulary for abstract concepts (e.g., 'social equality')
insights.title: Underdeveloped Abstract Vocabulary
insights.original_text: thereby promoting social equality.
insights.suggested_text: thereby reducing socioeconomic disparities and improving access to opportunities for all citizens.

insights.description: Simple sentence structures with occasional awkward phrasing
insights.title: Slight Overreliance on Simple Sentences
insights.original_text: However, some investment in roads remains essential, particularly in rural areas where alternatives are scarce.
insights.suggested_text: Nevertheless, road infrastructure remains vital in rural regions, where viable public transport alternatives are limited.

insights.description: Minor errors in article usage and prepositions
insights.title: Minor Article and Preposition Errors
insights.original_text: public funds would be better spent on public transport than on roads
insights.suggested_text: public funds would be more effectively allocated to public transport rather than road construction.

insights.description: Lack of variety in sentence structure and connectors
insights.title: Limited Sentence Variety
insights.original_text: On balance, priority should be given to public transport.
insights.suggested_text: In conclusion, public transport should receive greater investment than road expansion.

insights.description: Use of academic vocabulary with precision
insights.title: Precise Academic Terminology
insights.original_text: Induced demand ensures that expanded highways are rapidly saturated, rendering them a costly palliative
insights.suggested_text: Induced demand means that when roads are expanded, more people are likely to use them, quickly filling them up, making the investment a costly short-term solution.

insights.description: Clear and logical argument structure
insights.title: Structured Position with Balanced Counterpoint
insights.original_text: Admittedly, rural communities, for whom car ownership is a necessity rather than a choice, cannot be neglected; targeted road maintenance should therefore continue.
insights.suggested_text: However, in rural areas where car ownership is essential, road maintenance must continue to meet basic needs, though it should not dominate the budget.

insights.description: Use of cohesive devices and transitions
insights.title: Effective Cohesion via Logical Linking
insights.original_text: Nevertheless, the bulk of new expenditure ought to flow to collective transport.
insights.suggested_text: Therefore, most new spending should be directed toward public transport systems.

insights.description: Complex sentence structure with accurate grammar
insights.title: Sophisticated Sentence Construction
insights.original_text: Whether public money is better channelled into public transport or road infrastructure is, in my view, less a question of either/or than of strategic emphasis, though the evidence favours the former.
insights.suggested_text: In my view, the issue is not simply a choice between public transport and roads, but rather a question of strategic prioritization, and the evidence supports giving greater spending to public transport.

insights.description: Accuracy of formal register and tone
insights.title: Formal and Objective Tone
insights.original_text: the bulk of new expenditure ought to flow to collective transport
insights.suggested_text: a significant portion of new spending should be allocated to public transport systems

insights.description: Grammar – Subject-Verb Agreement & Article Errors
insights.title: Subject-Verb Agreement and Articles
insights.original_text: all student wear same clothes
insights.suggested_text: all students wear the same clothes

insights.description: Grammar – Incorrect Verb Form (Modal + Base Form)
insights.title: Modal + Base Verb Error
insights.original_text: I like wear my own clothes
insights.suggested_text: I like wearing my own clothes

insights.description: Grammar – Incorrect Preposition & Article
insights.title: Preposition and Plural Error
insights.original_text: is cheaper for parent
insights.suggested_text: is cheaper for parents

insights.description: Grammar – Run-on Sentence / Incorrect Structure
insights.title: Run-on Sentence Structure
insights.original_text: uniform is not comfortable in summer is very hot
insights.suggested_text: uniforms are not comfortable in summer because it is very hot

insights.description: Vocabulary – Basic & Repetitive
insights.title: Basic and Repetitive Vocabulary
insights.original_text: good
insights.suggested_text: promotes equality

insights.description: Style – Lack of Development & Depth
insights.title: Shallow Argument Development
insights.original_text: I think uniform is better for school
insights.suggested_text: I believe school uniforms help create a sense of equality and belonging, which supports a positive learning environment

insights.description: Cohesion – Missing Linking Words
insights.title: Missing Logical Transitions
insights.original_text: But sometimes... I like wear...
insights.suggested_text: However, in hot weather, uniforms can be uncomfortable. While I personally prefer wearing my own clothes, I still believe uniforms are beneficial for school life.

insights.description: Use of simple, functional vocabulary with limited academic or nuanced range
insights.title: Limited Lexical Range and Academic Tone
insights.original_text: In my opinion, school uniforms are a good idea for several reasons. First, they make all students look equal, so nobody feels bad about their clothes.
insights.suggested_text: In my view, school uniforms offer several benefits. Firstly, they promote equality among students, reducing feelings of social insecurity related to clothing.

insights.description: Lack of variety in sentence structures and grammar complexity
insights.title: Limited Grammatical Range and Sentence Variety
insights.original_text: However, some students say uniforms are uncomfortable and they cannot show their personality. I agree that this is a problem, but I think the advantages are more important.
insights.suggested_text: Nevertheless, some students find uniforms uncomfortable and feel they cannot express their individuality. While this concern is valid, the benefits of uniformity—such as reduced social division and cost savings—outweigh these drawbacks.

insights.description: Weak topic sentence development and insufficient paragraph structure
insights.title: Underdeveloped Paragraph Structure and Topic Sentences
insights.original_text: So, I think schools should keep uniforms.
insights.suggested_text: Therefore, I conclude that schools should maintain uniform policies, as the advantages of equality and financial responsibility outweigh the minor drawbacks.

insights.description: Missing depth of argument and balanced discussion
insights.title: Shallow Argument Development and Imbalanced Perspective
insights.original_text: I agree that this is a problem, but I think the advantages are more important.
insights.suggested_text: While it is true that uniforms may limit personal expression, the positive impact on student equality and parental financial burden is more significant, especially in diverse school environments.

insights.description: Grammar – Use of Complex Structures
insights.title: Replace informal phrases with academic verbs
insights.original_text: While some argue that school uniforms restrict individuality, I largely agree that they should be compulsory.
insights.suggested_text: While some claim that school uniforms undermine individuality, I firmly believe that they should be mandatory.

insights.description: Vocabulary – Precision and Academic Register
insights.title: Replace vague expressions with precise academic language
insights.original_text: students cannot compete over expensive brands
insights.suggested_text: students are less likely to face social pressure related to clothing choices

insights.description: Style – Development of Counterpoint
insights.title: Deepen counterargument with specific examples
insights.original_text: Admittedly, self-expression matters, yet students can still express themselves through hobbies and friendships.
insights.suggested_text: While individual expression is important, students can still demonstrate their personality through extracurricular activities and personal interests.

insights.description: Lexical Resource – Range and Variety
insights.title: Use precise, formal terms for financial and social concepts
insights.original_text: uniforms save families money in the long run, because children need fewer outfits.
insights.suggested_text: uniforms reduce household expenditure on clothing, as students require only a limited number of outfits.

insights.description: Coherence – Transition Flow
insights.title: Improve conclusion with explicit benefit listing
insights.original_text: In conclusion, the benefits of uniforms outweigh their drawbacks.
insights.suggested_text: In sum, the advantages of school uniforms—such as promoting equality and reducing financial burden—significantly outweigh the potential limitations.

insights.description: Vocabulary: Precision and Academic Register
insights.title: Replace Awkward Phrasing with Natural Idioms
insights.original_text: a standardised dress code, by contrast, levels the field without suppressing character, which tends to find its outlet in conversation, creativity and conduct rather than in clothing.
insights.suggested_text: a standardised dress code, by contrast, levels the playing field without undermining students' individuality, which is more fully expressed through conversation, creativity, and personal conduct.

insights.description: Grammar: Subordinate Clauses and Linking
insights.title: Use Natural and Common Verbs in Academic Contexts
insights.original_text: Where pupils are visibly differentiated by brand, schools inadvertently entrench socioeconomic divides;
insights.suggested_text: Where students are visibly differentiated by brand, schools inadvertently reinforce socioeconomic divides.

insights.description: Style: Nuance and Balance
insights.title: Refine Abstract Concepts for Clarity
insights.original_text: I am inclined to side with uniforms, chiefly because they neutralise the conspicuous consumption that otherwise taints adolescent peer relations.
insights.suggested_text: I am inclined to support school uniforms, primarily because they reduce the influence of conspicuous consumption in peer relationships.

insights.description: Cohesion: Logical Flow and Transitions
insights.title: Improve Flow with Stronger Transitional Phrases
insights.original_text: That said, uniforms should be affordable and climate-appropriate...
insights.suggested_text: However, for such a policy to be truly equitable, uniforms must be affordable and appropriate to the local climate.

insights.description: Limited topic development: The essay only briefly touches on advantages and disadvantages without fully discussing or elaborating on either.
insights.title: Lack of Development in Response to Prompt
insights.original_text: Many people work at home now. It is good because you not need go to office. You can sleep more and no traffic. But is bad too, because you are alone and no talk with friends. Sometimes the children make noise and I can't work. I think work at home is good one or two day in week.
insights.suggested_text: Many people now work from home. This shift has both benefits and drawbacks. On the positive side, remote work saves time and money—people avoid commuting and can save on office costs. It also allows greater flexibility, enabling individuals to manage personal responsibilities more effectively. However, disadvantages include reduced social interaction, potential isolation, and distractions at home, such as children or household noise. A balanced approach might involve working from home one or two days per week, combining flexibility with the benefits of office interaction.

insights.description: Inconsistent and incorrect grammar usage
insights.title: Incorrect Sentence Structure and Verb Forms
insights.original_text: you not need go to office
insights.suggested_text: you do not need to go to the office

insights.description: Use of simplistic and informal expressions
insights.title: Limited Vocabulary Range and Inappropriate Collocations
insights.original_text: you are alone and no talk with friends
insights.suggested_text: you feel isolated and miss opportunities for social interaction

insights.description: Poor use of cohesive devices and logical connections
insights.title: Missing Cohesive Links Between Ideas
insights.original_text: But is bad too, because you are alone and no talk with friends. Sometimes the children make noise and I can't work.
insights.suggested_text: However, this arrangement can lead to social isolation. Additionally, domestic distractions such as children playing can interfere with concentration and productivity.

insights.description: Inadequate task response – fails to fully address the prompt
insights.title: Incomplete Task Response
insights.original_text: I think work at home is good one or two day in week.
insights.suggested_text: In conclusion, while working from home offers convenience and flexibility, it also presents challenges such as isolation and distractions. A balanced approach—such as working remotely one or two days per week—may offer a practical solution.

insights.description: Use of simple sentence structures limits grammatical range and complexity.
insights.title: Limited Sentence Variety
insights.original_text: Nowadays more and more people work from home. One advantage is that they save time and money because they don't have to travel to the office. Another advantage is that they can organise their day more freely.
insights.suggested_text: Today, an increasing number of individuals are working from home. A major benefit is the significant time and cost savings achieved by eliminating daily commutes. Another advantage is greater flexibility in scheduling, allowing individuals to structure their workday according to personal preferences.

insights.description: Vocabulary is functional but lacks precision and academic tone.
insights.title: Basic Vocabulary with Limited Academic Register
insights.original_text: On the other hand, working at home can be lonely and some people find it difficult to separate work and private life.
insights.suggested_text: On the other hand, remote work may lead to feelings of isolation, and some individuals struggle to maintain a clear boundary between professional and personal responsibilities.

insights.description: Lack of development in arguments – surface-level points without explanation or examples.
insights.title: Shallow Analysis of Arguments
insights.original_text: In my opinion, the best solution is to work at home some days and in the office on other days.
insights.suggested_text: A balanced approach—such as hybrid work—may offer the best solution, combining the benefits of flexibility with the social and motivational advantages of in-person interaction.

insights.description: Missing clear linking devices and logical flow between ideas.
insights.title: Weak Linking and Flow
insights.original_text: One advantage is that they save time and money because they don't have to travel to the office. Another advantage is that they can organise their day more freely. On the other hand, working at home can be lonely...
insights.suggested_text: While remote work offers several advantages—such as time and cost savings and greater flexibility—there are also notable drawbacks. For instance, the absence of face-to-face interaction can lead to loneliness, and the blurred lines between work and personal time may result in burnout.

insights.description: Use of cohesive devices (e.g., 'on the positive side', 'nevertheless') to link ideas
insights.title: Effective Use of Cohesive Devices
insights.original_text: On the positive side, employees avoid long commutes, which saves time and reduces stress, and employers can cut the cost of office space. Nevertheless, there are notable disadvantages.
insights.suggested_text: On the positive side, employees avoid long commutes, which saves time and reduces stress; employers can also reduce office space costs. Nevertheless, there are notable disadvantages.

insights.description: Use of collocations and academic vocabulary (e.g., 'blur', 'burnout', 'flexibility', 'teamwork')
insights.title: Academic Vocabulary in Context
insights.original_text: Workers may feel isolated from colleagues, and the boundary between professional and personal life can blur, leading to burnout.
insights.suggested_text: Workers may feel isolated from their colleagues, and the boundary between work and personal life can blur, leading to burnout.

insights.description: Variety and precision in sentence structures (simple and compound sentences only)
insights.title: Limited Sentence Variety
insights.original_text: Remote working has become increasingly common, and it brings both benefits and drawbacks.
insights.suggested_text: Remote working has become increasingly common, offering both significant benefits and notable drawbacks.

insights.description: Clarity and logical flow of argument with a clear opinion
insights.title: Clear Opinion with Balanced View
insights.original_text: Overall, I believe a hybrid arrangement offers the most sensible balance, since it preserves flexibility without sacrificing teamwork.
insights.suggested_text: Overall, I believe a hybrid model offers the most balanced solution—preserving flexibility while maintaining effective teamwork.

insights.description: Use of sophisticated academic register and formal tone
insights.title: Formal and Academic Diction
insights.original_text: The widespread shift towards remote work has been hailed as a liberation from the tyranny of the commute
insights.suggested_text: The growing trend of remote work has been praised as a way to escape the stress of daily commutes

insights.description: Effective use of contrast and balance between advantages and disadvantages
insights.title: Balanced Argumentation
insights.original_text: Undoubtedly, flexibility enhances autonomy and, by dispersing the workforce, eases pressure on urban housing and transport. Conversely, the erosion of informal interaction... can quietly impoverish organisational culture
insights.suggested_text: Remote work offers clear benefits, such as greater flexibility and reduced demand on city housing and transport. However, it also undermines workplace culture through the loss of informal interactions.

insights.description: Precise vocabulary use with academic synonyms (e.g., 'tyranny', 'erode', 'impoverish')
insights.title: Advanced Lexical Choice
insights.original_text: the tyranny of the commute, the erosion of informal interaction, the absence of physical boundaries tempts employees to be perpetually available
insights.suggested_text: the burden of daily commutes, the loss of casual workplace chats, and the lack of physical separation that leads to constant availability

insights.description: Complex sentence structures with subordinate clauses and collocations
insights.title: Complex Sentence Structures
insights.original_text: A deliberately structured hybrid model therefore seems preferable to either extreme.
insights.suggested_text: Therefore, a carefully designed hybrid model is better than either full remote or full office work.

insights.description: Use of cohesive devices (e.g., 'conversely', 'therefore') to link ideas logically
insights.title: Effective Cohesion
insights.original_text: Undoubtedly, flexibility enhances autonomy... Conversely, the erosion of informal interaction...
insights.suggested_text: While flexibility improves work-life balance, the loss of spontaneous workplace conversations may harm team cohesion.

insights.description: Simple sentence structure with minimal variation
insights.title: Limited Sentence Variation
insights.original_text: I think government must spend more money for public transport. Bus and train is good for people because is cheap.
insights.suggested_text: I believe governments should prioritize public transport spending. Buses and trains are beneficial because they are affordable for most people.

insights.description: Inconsistent verb forms and article usage
insights.title: Incorrect Verb Forms and Articles
insights.original_text: Bus and train is good for people because is cheap. Many people have not car.
insights.suggested_text: Buses and trains are useful because they are inexpensive. Many people do not own cars.

insights.description: Lack of logical development or argument structure
insights.title: Absence of Clear Argument Structure
insights.original_text: Roads are important too but too many car make air bad and traffic jam. In my city the bus is old and slow, so people don't like it. Government should buy new bus.
insights.suggested_text: While roads are essential, the increasing number of private vehicles leads to pollution and traffic congestion. In my city, outdated buses contribute to poor public transport experiences. Therefore, the government should invest in modern, efficient public transport systems.

insights.description: Inappropriate or vague vocabulary
insights.title: Inappropriate or Vague Vocabulary
insights.original_text: Bus and train is good for people because is cheap.
insights.suggested_text: Buses and trains are beneficial because they are affordable and accessible to most citizens.

insights.description: Missing counterarguments or balanced view
insights.title: Lack of Balanced Perspective
insights.original_text: I think government must spend more money for public transport. ... Roads are important too but too many car make air bad and traffic jam.
insights.suggested_text: While I agree that governments should spend more on public transport, I acknowledge that roads remain vital for emergency services and private vehicle access. However, over-reliance on personal vehicles leads to environmental and traffic problems.

insights.description: Factual inaccuracies or overgeneralizations
insights.title: Overgeneralization and Lack of Specificity
insights.original_text: In my city the bus is old and slow, so people don't like it.
insights.suggested_text: In my city, public transport services have been underfunded, leading to aging fleets and long waiting times, which reduces public confidence.

insights.description: Basic linking words limit cohesion and flow
insights.title: Use of Basic Linking Words
insights.original_text: Firstly, public transport is cheaper... Secondly, fewer cars means less pollution...
insights.suggested_text: Public transport is not only more affordable for everyday citizens, but it also significantly reduces traffic congestion. Furthermore, when fewer private vehicles are used, urban traffic patterns become more efficient.

insights.description: Vague expressions reduce precision and depth
insights.title: Avoid Vague Phrases with Specific Language
insights.original_text: public transport is cheaper for ordinary people
insights.suggested_text: public transport is significantly more affordable than private car ownership for low- to middle-income households

insights.description: Lack of complex sentence structures limits grammatical range
insights.title: Develop Sentence Variety and Complexity
insights.original_text: But if the government builds more roads, there will be more cars, so the problem will not disappear.
insights.suggested_text: If new roads are constructed without corresponding investment in public transport, the incentive to own a car may increase, leading to a cycle of congestion and pollution that worsens over time.

insights.description: Limited vocabulary range and precision
insights.title: Expand Lexical Range with Precise Terminology
insights.original_text: less pollution, which is good for health
insights.suggested_text: reduced emissions of harmful pollutants such as carbon monoxide and nitrogen oxides, which directly impact respiratory health

insights.description: Inadequate handling of counterarguments
insights.title: Improve Response to Counterpoints
insights.original_text: Of course, roads are still necessary, for example for ambulances and delivery trucks.
insights.suggested_text: While roads remain essential for emergency services and logistics, public transport infrastructure can serve a broader range of users without compromising access to these vital services.

insights.description: Conclusion lacks depth and closure
insights.title: Strengthen Conclusion with a Clear Summary
insights.original_text: For these reasons I agree with the statement.
insights.suggested_text: In conclusion, prioritizing public transport over road expansion is a more sustainable and equitable long-term solution for urban mobility.

insights.description: Clear position with balanced argument
insights.title: Strong Position with Balanced View
insights.original_text: I broadly share this view.
insights.suggested_text: I agree with this view to a significant extent.

insights.description: Effective use of logical reasoning
insights.title: Logical Cause-Effect Reasoning
insights.original_text: Building additional roads tends to encourage more car use, so congestion soon returns
insights.suggested_text: The construction of new roads often leads to induced demand, where more people buy cars, causing congestion to return quickly.

insights.description: Use of a relevant social benefit
insights.title: Social Equality Benefit
insights.original_text: affordable public transport benefits those who cannot afford a car, thereby promoting social equality
insights.suggested_text: accessible public transport helps reduce inequality by providing affordable mobility options for low-income individuals.

insights.description: Acknowledgment of counterpoint
insights.title: Balanced Counterargument
insights.original_text: However, some investment in roads remains essential, particularly in rural areas where alternatives are scarce.
insights.suggested_text: That said, road infrastructure remains vital in rural regions where public transport is either unavailable or unreliable.

insights.description: Appropriate conclusion
insights.title: Clear, Concise Conclusion
insights.original_text: On balance, priority should be given to public transport.
insights.suggested_text: Therefore, public transport should be given greater priority in government spending.

insights.description: Use of cohesive devices
insights.title: Effective Cohesive Devices
insights.original_text: Furthermore, affordable public transport benefits...
insights.suggested_text: Furthermore, accessible public transport not only benefits individuals but also contributes to broader social equity.

insights.description: Simple but accurate sentence structures
insights.title: Clear Sentence Structure
insights.original_text: Building additional roads tends to encourage more car use, so congestion soon returns
insights.suggested_text: New road construction often leads to increased car usage, which results in congestion resurfacing.

insights.description: Limited range of vocabulary
insights.title: Basic Lexical Range
insights.original_text: public transport, roads, affordable, social equality
insights.suggested_text: public transit, road infrastructure, accessibility, social equity, urban mobility

insights.description: Minor grammatical issues
insights.title: Minor Article/Preposition Use
insights.original_text: affordable public transport benefits those who cannot afford a car
insights.suggested_text: affordable public transport benefits individuals who lack access to private vehicles

insights.description: Use of academic vocabulary and precision in argumentation
insights.title: Precise Academic Terminology
insights.original_text: the evidence favours the former
insights.suggested_text: the evidence strongly supports prioritizing public transport

insights.description: Effective use of contrast and concession structures
insights.title: Balancing arguments with logical transitions
insights.original_text: Admittedly, rural communities...cannot be neglected; targeted road maintenance should therefore continue.
insights.suggested_text: However, in rural areas where car ownership is essential, targeted road maintenance must remain a priority.

insights.description: Use of complex sentence structures with subordination
insights.title: Subordinate clauses and conditional logic
insights.original_text: Induced demand ensures that expanded highways are rapidly saturated, rendering them a costly palliative, whereas rail and bus networks deliver durable gains in capacity, emissions and equity of access.
insights.suggested_text: Due to induced demand, expanded highways quickly reach capacity and become a costly solution; in contrast, rail and bus systems offer sustainable improvements in capacity, emissions, and access equity.

insights.description: Appropriate use of formal tone and argument balance
insights.title: Avoiding overstatement and maintaining neutrality
insights.original_text: the bulk of new expenditure ought to flow to collective transport
insights.suggested_text: a significant portion of new spending should be directed toward public transport systems
